title: The Missing Granite
note: Placeholder authored text (owner review pending). A dispute between the mason and a carrier over stone that never arrived. Narrative-only but for one real ware: backing the mason costs the warehouse a load of granite (the keeper hands it over). The cast is the settlement's own people.

effects.text: The Missing Granite: I took the mason's side. The keeper gave {mason} a load of granite from the store.

lines: Granite from the store, on your word. I will not forget who stood up for me, wizard. The hearth will be finished by the week's end.
You took {hauler}'s word over mine. Fine. I will fetch my own stone from now on, and the hearth can wait.

effects.text: The Missing Granite: I worked out where the load went. Nobody was lying; the store had it all along.

lines: Under the grout sacks. The whole time. I owe {hauler} a word, and you a drink.
Stone is stone. We are past it.
Do you see this wall? No, you do not, because there is no wall, because there is no granite. {hauler} swears a load was carried in. I say it never came.
Six loads were due from the quarry. Five came. {hauler} carried the sixth, {hauler} says. I have five, and a hearth with a hole in it.

choices.text: I believe you. I will ask the keeper for a load from the store.
lines: Then I will stop shouting. Thank you.
So the store pays for what I carried and {mason} gets to call me a liar for free. Good to know how it works.

effects.text: The Missing Granite: I took the carrier's side. {mason} will have to fetch the stone again.

lines: Thank you. Nobody believes a carrier. We only walk the roads all day, what would we know about what is on them.
Under the grout. I put it there myself and forgot; the keeper had me stacking grout all morning. I will go and say so.
Roads to walk. Was there something?
If this is about the granite, I carried it. In through the north door, down on the floor, done. Whatever {mason} did with it after is {mason}'s affair.

choices.text: What happened to the sixth load?
lines: I carried it. The keeper was shouting about grout sacks that morning, everything went everywhere, but the stone went in. I am not a thief and I am not a fool.

choices.text: I believe you. The mason can fetch the stone again.
lines: Then I will walk a little lighter today.

choices.text: Grout sacks, you said. Where does the keeper stack grout?

lines: By the north door. Where I put the... oh. Oh, no. Under the grout. It will be under the grout.
All over the place, that morning. I could not tell you.

choices.text: I will let you get on.
